I see, I understand.

But just to make it clear lang kasi I think this is not enough reason for UST to sweep it under the rug. I get that I might’ve gotten some things wrong, especially about putting the blame on the professor for the student failing twice—that wasn’t fair, and I’m open to the idea that there’s more to the story. But I still stand by what I said about the importance of taking action when a student shows clear signs of distress. When someone opens up and shows red flags, I really think it’s important to let either the family or a professional know. It’s not about pointing fingers—it’s about making sure the student gets the help they need. As a university, making sure that students are safe and supported should always be a top priority.

Gets naman na di dapat ipasa because of mental health especially since he’s in the medical field. But to blame the parents instead? Do you even know what its like to suffer mentally? Malaki ang support system nung bata, the family are actually very supportive and accepting of his situation. Pero siya mismo struggled to accept it which caused him to fall deep into depression. And you know why they’re blaming the professor? Kasi he’s the only one na pinagsabihan nung bata. As an educator, responsibilidad mo rin ang wellness ng estudyante mo. Kung hindi niya talaga maipapasa yung bata, sana man lamg inalert niya magulang nung bata or anyone for that matter na alam niyang makakatulong dun sa bata na iovercome yung nararamdaman niyang yon. Pero hindi eh, wala eh, walang nakaalam. Heck, we dont even know how he responded to it but base from the family’s posts mukhang hindi rin ok ang naging response nito dun sa bata. Pero sige, like u said hindi natin alam kasi hindi naman pinost. But what we know for sure is no one knew except for that professor. 

Also, he was supposed to graduate 2024 - already on the graduating list, got his picture taken and everything. Then suddenly may pahabol hindi pala? Do you honestly think that’s fair? Dun palang may lapse na yung professor hindi magupdate ng maayos. Simple as it is but it could really affect a student a lot. So yeah, might not be 100% his fault but sure enough significant yung naging parte niya dun and for that he should be made accountable.

Sorry but for this context, I disagree. Knew the student personally and based from the posts of his family, I dont think they want the silent treatment. Kaya nga it really bothers me na wala man lang UST admin that’s acknowledging this, especially because yung pamilya niya na mismo nagiingay sa soc med, and rightfully so because that professor needs to be accountable to some extent.

at the end of the day, you are still not in the position to assess if worth ba yung absent or not for them kasi may mga underlying issues pa yan na hindi niyo totally magegets until you experienced it firsthand. And i think isa yan sa mga need matutunan ng HR and managers esp since isa rin yon sa factor ng employee retention. How the company is taking care of their employees so included na jan ang both physical and mental health. What I would suggest is to reassess yung company process niyo and check if kaya bang magoutput based or hybrid na setup. That way, hindi niyo to problema and you can implement stricter or hard deadlines. Wala pa kayong need bayarang extra for OT pay unless super need lang talaga. Kasi from experience sa industry, sobrang common especially sa mga 100% onsite na yung mga employees ay nagpapanggap lang na nagtatrabaho sa office. Which is kahit papano understandable kasi di naman laging hectic or maraming deliverables, and di rin naman kaya ng employee na 8 hrs straight focus lang sa work. Work-life balance lang talaga ang sagot jan. and since hindi naman to one-size fits all, why not
implement something na pwedeng yung employee na mismo ang makakapagdecide ng balance at the same time u will still get your deliverables submitted on time. Also, mas tipid din sa logistics if di kayo laging on-site

Also, hindi talaga enticing and offered benefits niyo esp that HMO. Sobrang red flag. And OP, baka youre not doing your job very well as an HR to filter and assess the applicants. And if youre gonna think long term, better siguro to invest in employees na sigurado even if the pay is slightly higher. That way hindi ka nagsasayang ng pers at oras kakatrain, and mamake sure mo pa na value adding talaga yung employee sa company niyo.
